messages.subject: Area transition rates
parts:
Hi BioGeo Group,

Does anyone know a way quantify the number of transitions into/out of each area? I want to test the hypothesis that an environmental barrier between two areas precludes recolonization of ancestral areas as a result of specialization. Once a lineage specializes enough to colonize area C it is less likely/able to diverge back into B or A. 

Any insight on how to test this or general advice on analyzing transition dynamics from BioGeoBEARs output would be greatly appreciated.

Best,
Chauncey

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Area transition rates
parts:
Hi! The "easiest" way to do this would be Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping -- google it for the script etc. You would get a sample of histories, each one as a table of events, and then go through those tables and count up the dispersal events and their directionality etc.  You could also do this under several different models and compare them.

The hard part is understanding the table structure and figuring out how to use R to e.g. count events in a table. This isn't "hard", but there is no tutorial written on it, it mostly depends on general R skills, so if you are willing to invest some time you can make it work.

Cheers!
Nick
